section_summary: This section contains diplomatic correspondence, memoranda, and a cross-reference file note from 1938 to 1941 concerning alleged copyright infringement and unauthorized publications of American works in Japan. It details attempts by author W. Jefferson Davis to secure royalties from Japanese publishers for an unauthorized translation of his book, noting the lack of translation protection under the 1905 U.S.-Japan copyright convention, alongside a reference to an unauthorized film adaptation of Margaret Mitchell's 'Gone With the Wind'. In addition, the section covers protests by the Reinhold Publishing Corporation regarding the direct English-language offset reproduction and sale of Carleton Ellis's 'The Chemistry of Petroleum Derivatives' by a Tokyo firm.

subfiles.about: The American Embassy reports on discussions with Mr. Kawarada and publisher Seibun-do regarding royalty claims for the unauthorized Japanese translation of W. Jefferson Davis's book.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Counselor of Embassy, American Embassy, Tokyo (for the Ambassador)
subfiles.summary: Counselor Dooman reports Seibun-do's rejection of Davis's royalty demands, recommending a small settlement given Japan's narrow publishing profits and questionable legal protection.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Tokyo Embassy Regarding Unauthorized Translation of W. Jefferson Davis's Book

subfiles.about: The Department of State transmits the substance of the Tokyo Embassy's report concerning settlement negotiations for the unauthorized Japanese translation of W. Jefferson Davis's book.
subfiles.from: Wallace McClure, Assistant Chief, Treaty Division (for the Secretary of State)
keywords: Japan, the Air Menace of the Pacific
subfiles.summary: Wallace McClure transmits the Tokyo Embassy's report on Seibun-do's refusal of Davis's royalty demand, suggesting a small settlement and inviting comment.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Stephen P. Ladas Regarding Unauthorized Translation of 'Japan, the Air Menace of the Pacific'
subfiles.to: Stephen P. Ladas, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum records a telephone inquiry from W. Jefferson Davis regarding copyright protection and royalties for his book unauthorizedly published in Japan.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Treaty Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Department officials informed Davis that treaties provide no protection against unauthorized translation, while Davis sought royalties through the Japanese Ambassador.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Telephone Conversation with W. Jefferson Davis Concerning Copyright Piracy in Japan

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing a letter from author Margaret Mitchell concerning a pirated movie adaptation of 'Gone With the Wind' being produced in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Margaret Mitchell's letter regarding an unauthorized Japanese film adaptation of 'Gone With the Wind'.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note for Letter from Margaret Mitchell Concerning Pirated Movie of 'Gone With the Wind'

subfiles.about: The Department of State cites the 1905 copyright convention and inquires whether the pirated Japanese edition of Carleton Ellis's book is in English or Japanese.
subfiles.from: Department of State (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: The Department cites the 1905 copyright convention, inquiring whether the unauthorized edition is in English or Japanese to determine feasible action.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to C. C. Robinson Regarding Alleged Infringement of 'Chemistry of Petroleum Derivatives'
subfiles.to: C. C. Robinson, Manager, Book Dept., Reinhold Publishing Corporation

subfiles.about: Reinhold Publishing Corporation informs the State Department that Carleton Ellis's work was reproduced in English by offset printing and requests immediate intervention.
subfiles.from: C. C. Robinson, Manager, Book Dept., Reinhold Publishing Corporation
subfiles.summary: Robinson confirms Ellis's book was duplicated in English by offset process, violating the 1905 convention, and urges immediate protective action.
subfiles.title: Letter from C. C. Robinson to Wallace McClure Regarding English Offset Reproduction of Ellis's Book in Japan
subfiles.to: Wallace McClure, Acting Chief, Treaty Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: Reinhold Publishing Corporation reports that Gohin Seisakujo of Tokyo is reprinting Carleton Ellis's chemistry treatise without authorization and seeks State Department advice.
subfiles.from: C. C. Robinson, Manager, Book Dept., Reinhold Publishing Corporation
subfiles.summary: Robinson reports Gohin Seisakujo's unauthorized reprinting of Ellis's chemistry work in Tokyo, asking the State Department for guidance on protective procedures.
subfiles.title: Letter from C. C. Robinson to Wallace McClure Reporting Unauthorized Japanese Reprint by Gohin Seisakujo
subfiles.to: Dr. Wallace McClure, Assistant Chief, Treaty Division, Department of State
